title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 51–53). Grothendieck is building an axiomatic theory of 'ateliers'. An atelier A is a set of 'figures' with an inclusion order and a binary relation written X |·| Y, subject to axioms Ax 1–4. Each atelier A has an associated set of 'points' Σ_A. Conversely, each base Σ carrying an order ≤ and a structure C (an 'organisation', p. 53) yields an atelier Atspat(Σ) (the reading 'Atspl' is uncertain; p. 53 writes Atopat/Atopos). Its elements are pairs X = (Φ, ρ): a finite part Φ ⊂ Σ with an order ρ, and Φ has a greatest element X^0.

Page 51 checks Ax 1–4 for A = Atspat(Σ). It then defines A → Σ, X ↦ X^0, and shows the relation |·| on A induces the relation on Σ. This gives an injection Σ_A → Σ_Σ = Σ. It also gives a section Σ → A, x ↦ ({x}, ρ_x), with Σ → A → Σ equal to the identity.

This page.
(1) Hence Σ_A ≃ Σ_Σ ≃ Σ, and the identification respects the order and the structure C. In words: the points of the spatial atelier built on Σ are recovered as Σ.
(2) Therefore the canonical map A → Atspat(Σ_A) becomes, via Σ_A ≃ Σ, the composite A → Atspat(Σ_A) ≅ Atspat(Σ) = A, which is the identity. So for A = Atspat(Σ) the canonical map is bijective, not merely injective.
(3) General case. For an arbitrary atelier A, set Σ = Σ_A. There is a canonical morphism of ateliers A → Atspat(Σ), X ↦ Disp(X), even when A is not spatial. It is 'faithful': X |·| Y ⟺ Disp(X) |·| Disp(Y). The sentence 'Dire que A est spatial signifie …' continues on p. 53: A is identified, through this injective functor, with a sub-structure of Atopat(Σ). So A amounts to data (≤, C, A) with A ⊂ Atopat(Σ) closed under a certain operation, plus a substitute for the axiom 'Ateliers 2' (∀x, {{x}} ∈ A).

Modern reading. This is a representation/spatiality theorem of Stone or locale type.
- Every atelier maps faithfully to the 'spatial' atelier built on its points.
- Spatial ateliers are those for which this map identifies A with a sub-atelier.
- The construction Σ ↦ Atspat(Σ) is idempotent: points of Atspat(Σ) give back Σ, and the unit is an isomorphism on Atspat(Σ).

This mirrors the unit/counit of the points–opens adjunction between locales and spaces (spatial locales, sober spaces), or Stone's representation of a lattice in the power set of its prime filters. Its purpose is to reduce the abstract notion of atelier to concrete 'figure' data over a base organisation Σ. This continues chapter VIII, where 'ensembliste' ateliers were treated relative to a base set L.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The key step 'canonical map identifies with identity ⇒ bijective' is correct, given the p. 51 facts that Σ_A → Σ is injective and has a section (so it is bijective) and that it respects the order and C (asserted, not checked here).
The faithfulness claim X |·| Y ⟺ Disp X |·| Disp Y is asserted without proof on this page; whether it holds for every atelier depends on Ax 1–4, which are not visible here.

ideas.what: The points Σ_A of the spatial atelier Atspat(Σ) recover Σ (Σ_A ≃ Σ_Σ ≃ Σ), and the canonical map A → Atspat(Σ_A) is bijective for spatial A.
ideas.modern_name: Idempotence of a points/spatialization adjunction; unit is an isomorphism on spatial objects
ideas.usually_credited_to: Stone (1936–37) for Boolean algebras and distributive lattices; Ehresmann, Bénabou, Isbell, Johnstone for locales and sober spaces
ideas.where_published: Analogous to the SGA 4 discussion of points of topoi ('topos ayant suffisamment de points', Deligne's theorem); the atelier version appears unpublished.

ideas.what: Faithful canonical morphism A → Atspat(Σ_A), X ↦ Disp(X), for an arbitrary atelier; 'spatial' means this identifies A with a sub-atelier.
ideas.modern_name: Spatial reflection / representation theorem (spatial locale, enough points)

missed.claim: The axiomatic theory of 'ateliers' over an 'organisation' (Σ, ≤, C) has no published counterpart. It aims at a representation of abstract combinatorial-geometric structures (sets of figures with a relation |·|) as families of ordered finite figures on a base of points, with a spatiality criterion and point recovery. As a body of definitions it is undocumented, but this page itself only proves the routine Stone-type idempotence step.
missed.quote: cette application canonique est donc non seulement injective, mais bijection!
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents Grothendieck's 1986 'point-set-free' foundations program (ateliers, organisations). This could interest historians and anyone reconstructing his late combinatorial foundations; the result on this page is not new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a standard Stone/locale-type spatiality-and-points argument transplanted to Grothendieck's private 'atelier' framework. The framework is unpublished and somewhat interesting historically, but the mathematics on the page is routine.
transcription_corrections: The faithfulness line reads 'X |·| Y ⟺ Disp(X) |·| Disp Y' (the relation |·|), not 'X ⊂ Y ⟺ Disp(X) ⊂ Disp Y'.
'Atspl' is more likely 'Atspat' (atelier spatial); the next page has 'Atopat'.
'à l'application identique' should be read as '[est] l'application identique': the composite is the identity.
The struck passage reads roughly 'Alors A [est] isomorphe comme sous-atelier de Atsp(Σ)', with 'morphisme d'ateliers' added above, then crossed out.
'C'est un morphisme fidèle, i.e.' is correctly read; the next line begins 'Dire que A est spatial, signifie'.
The line before 'de C.' may read 'et on voit que [ce morphisme] respecte les relations d'ordre et de C' rather than 'ses morphismes relativement à des'; uncertain.
